title: [SOP TITLE LINE ONE

purpose: [One or two sentences: what this SOP does, who it is for, and the outcome it protects.]

meta.category: [Operations Manual category, e.g. Day-to-Day Operating Requirements]
meta.section: [Chapter number and name, e.g. Chapter 5.5 — Customer service standards]
meta.appliesTo: [Roles, teams and sites this SOP applies to]
meta.reportingOwner: [Name, review cadence; who makes resourcing / timing decisions]

howToUse: [Two to three sentences. State that this is a working procedure, not a guideline, and name the two or three non-negotiables the reader must take away. Say who raises, who confirms, and who owns the outcome.]
intro: [Paragraph 1: what this SOP sets out and across which sites or teams.]
[Paragraph 2: what happened before this process existed, and what this SOP replaces it with. Keep it factual.]
[Paragraph 3: where this document sits in the Operations Manual and which companion documents it should be read alongside.]
introNote: [If this process itself is not working, say who to raise it with first, then who owns the SOP.]

standards.intro: [One to two sentences: these are the non-negotiable standards, enforced structurally wherever possible rather than relying on individual discretion.]
rows: [Requirement. Specific, measurable, no override path unless stated.]
standards.keyRule: [The single definition or threshold people most often get wrong. State what counts, and what does not, in plain terms.]

roles.intro: [One to two sentences: every task has one named owner at all times. The table sets out who is responsible, who can reassign, and who to escalate to if something is not moving.]
roles.procedureNote: [Practical reminder: the most common failure point, and what happens if it is missed.]

metrics.intro: [One to two sentences: the metrics below confirm the process is working as intended and catch problems before they become a pattern.]
metrics.reviewOwner: [Who reviews which metrics, how often, and who decides when a standard is found to be unworkable. State that this SOP will be updated to reflect any change.]

steps: [Step one. Name the system, page or form to open.]
resources: [Companion document or guide, and where it lives]
[System or access issues: contact name / role]

onepager.purpose: [One sentence: what this SOP makes happen, and for whom.]
onepager.keyRule: [The one rule people most often get wrong, in one sentence.]

poster._comment: Optional. Only when a wall poster earns its place. layout 'A' carries the whole SOP in condensed form (the fields below); layout 'B' is a flow poster: replace everything below with { layout:'B', purpose, accentSecondLine, stops:[{owner, stage, standard, icon, key}], keyRule, fullSopRef }. icons: queue, menu, card, screen, flame, tick, bag, table. Layout B holds at most 8 stops, stage names 1 to 3 words, standard under 60 characters.
